text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Sierra Leone coup leaders demand $46 million to flee the country before the deposed elected president can return to his post.
- Local flights back to normal after they were paralysed on Monday by shortage of aviation fuel.
- State oil firm NNPC promises relief from fuel shortage.
- Four French trade missions are expected in Nigeria before the end of this year, says industries minister Lieutenant-General Mohammed Haladu.
- Navy flagship heads for Sierra Leone as Nigeria deploys two more warships to join a West African force striving to flush out soldiers who seized power in a coup on May 25th.

- Umbrella opposition NADECO group says there will be no overt commemoration of the annulled June 12 1993 presidential election on Thursday while police warn that they would not allow any demonstrations.
- Despite complaints of unfavourable business climate, Nigerian companies are declaring good invesment returns going by their corporate reports.
- Nigeria's inflation rate has fallen to 18.5 percent at the end of April from 22.4 percent at the end of March, says finance minister Anthony Ani at a seminar in Abuja.

- Federal government may have quietly barred rallies planned by a pro-government group for Thursday to call on military ruler General Sani Abacha to contest next year's election and turn himself into an elected president, sources say.
